data.long_meaning: From the Polish word ‘felicja’ which means happiness or joy. In the Christian tradition, Feliksa is believed to represent the shining light of God’s grace and love. The name Feliksa carries the meaning “Bright, shining light” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Feliksa usually hope their child will grow to embody bright, shining light and live with faith, good character and purpose.

historical_references.reference: Saint Felicitas, a Roman martyr, is believed to have been a slave girl who was beheaded along with her mother, Perpetua, and two brothers, Saturus and Perpetua. They were put to death in AD 203 during the reign of Emperor Septimius Severus. Felicitas is venerated as a saint in the Catholic Church and is the patroness of women seeking to enter religious communities.

Feliksa of Poland, born as Helena of Węgrzynowice, was a Polish nun and mystic who lived during the 15th century. She is best known for her visions and revelations, which she recorded in a book called the 'Revelations of the Virgin Mary to Feliksa of Poland'. Feliksa's visions were believed to provide guidance and consolation to the people of Poland during a time of political and religious upheaval, and she is considered a patroness of Poland and a model of Christian faith and devotion.
